historical_references.reference: According to tradition, Thekla was a martyr in the 3rd century, born in Cilicia in Asia Minor. She was the daughter of a high-ranking Roman officer named Theophilus. Thekla was a devoted follower of Saint Paul and accompanied him on his missionary journeys. After Paul's death, she went to Myra in Lycia, where she was later arrested for her faith and sentenced to be burnt at the stake. Thekla survived the ordeal and was eventually beheaded, around 235 CE.

Thekla is also known from the 'Acts of Thekla', an early Christian apocryphal text that dates to the 4th or 5th century. This text recounts the miraculous events of Thekla's life, including her visions, healings, and rescues. It describes Thekla as a strong and independent woman, whose faith and devotion to Saint Paul helped her overcome various challenges and obstacles.
